brief: Goldman's Brian Garrett flags non-fundamental headwinds the market must digest in the near term. Short-term CTA thresholds across NDX, SPX and RTY all broke on the morning of 10 September, in addition to a European index that broke down earlier in the week. The desk models resulting systematic supply at -23bn over one week and -28bn over one month, and states those figures do not incorporate the pre-market sell-off. VIX tends to sit near 25 when this type of technical deterioration happens, against 17 currently. Gamma at spot remains supportive because the street is long, but on a roughly 200 basis point further selloff the desk models a flip from positive to negative gamma. Global systematic positioning across CTA, vol control and risk parity is estimated at $421 billion of global equity exposure, close to five-year highs. The note presents model levels, threshold breaks and modelled supply. It does not argue a target or an index path.
